description: Known-answer labels for the synthetic sample papers (T-11). Labels describe what a human reader finds in the paper content, independent of section headings. Drafted with AI assistance (Claude, 2026-10-19) and to be reviewed by the student; written by the same party as the rules, so NOT an independent ground truth (see issues I-009, I-018).

label_definitions.present: The paper reports the element with enough detail to check or repeat it.
label_definitions.weak: The element is mentioned but without the detail needed to check or repeat it.

C1: RQ1 and RQ2 stated in the introduction
C2: 24 projects, 18,240 executions, labelling rule, project-wise split, licenses
C3: Python/scikit-learn versions, hyperparameters, hardware, three-step procedure

C1: only a claim ('we show that ML can make reviews faster'), no objective or question
C2: 'various open-source projects' - source named vaguely, no size or selection
C3: 'standard settings and appropriate parameters' - setup mentioned without detail
C5: 'better than existing tools' - comparison claimed, no baseline named
C8: no code/data availability; 'open-source projects' describes the data, not the artifact

C1: 'The goal of this study is to measure...'
C3: power meter, 4-core CPU, 16 GB RAM, three tools per repository
C4: energy in joules and wall-clock latency
